purpose: Milestones that exist AFTER the pinned Phase 1 package, declared by this repository rather than by the package.
why_this_file_exists: tools/partial_closures.py derives every gate name from the pinned requirements package, and that is right: a completing gate a requirement does not name is a completer nobody agreed to. But the package specifies PHASE 1, and it names M0 through M6. Every one of them has landed.

Three partial closures terminate in something no gate of Phase 1 can produce: ink leaving a real printer. FR-FUL-008 (allergy salience surviving physical printing), FR-FUL-014 (physical printing and deduplication) and FR-BIL-017 (paper out of a physical machine) are one hardware dependency wearing three faces. Everything up to the last inch is built and proved; the paper is not a thing this repository can observe.

They could not be closed honestly — this register's own FR-INT-007 entry refused to close on 'a transport now exists' because that would record an untested path as exercised — and they could not be moved, because there was nowhere unlanded to move them to.

So the milestone is declared HERE rather than edited into the package. Two reasons. The package's sha256 is quoted in README.md and planning/ARCHITECTURE_CONFORMANCE_PLAN.md as the pin; editing the package would make both statements false while nothing checked. And a pilot that happens after Phase 1 is not part of the Phase 1 specification — it is a fact about how this repository intends to finish, which is exactly what planning/ holds.

It is a FILE rather than a list inside tools/partial_closures.py for the reason that tool avoids lists: a hardcoded gate in the checker is a second source of truth the checker cannot see changing. A declaration here is derived from, reviewable on its own, and visible in a diff.
how_a_milestone_here_closes: It cannot land from this repository. landed_gates() reads tests/ and matches m<digit><letter>, so no directory name can make PILOT landed, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight: a milestone whose evidence is a physical act should not be closable by adding a test file.
An entry naming PILOT closes when somebody runs the thing on real hardware and records what they observed in closed_by_evidence, naming the machine and what came out of it.

milestones.name: Pilot on real hardware
milestones.purpose: Verify the aspects of Phase 1 whose evidence is physical: paper leaving a printer, and anything else no build can observe.
milestones.exit_criterion: A receipt and a station ticket come out of a supported production printer at a real outlet, legible, with allergy emphasis intact and no duplicate on retry across a restart.
